title: Flat local maps with regular source and fibre have regular target
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume that $R$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], that the closed fibre $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular, and that $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $S$ is regular.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre); its proof uses Lemma Tag 00ON (dimension-base-fibre-equals-total)

proof.text: The regular closed-fibre hypothesis supplies its Noetherian and local instances [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Write I = m_R S. Locality gives comap(f,m_S) = m_R and I ≤ m_S. The surjective quotient map q : S → S/I sends m_S to the unique maximal ideal of the closed fibre. This uses the standard local-ring map and quotient APIs, not a separate Noetherian-image theorem.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre), lines 27458--27468: the setting of the statement, made explicit

proof.text: Equip S with the R-algebra structure from f. Flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] supplies going down. The comap equality makes m_S lie over m_R. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula], Mathlib Ideal.height_eq_height_add_of_liesOver_of_hasGoingDown, to these two maximal ideals. Rewrite the quotient image using IsLocalRing.map_maximalIdeal_of_surjective, and rewrite all maximal-ideal heights as Krull dimensions using IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_height_eq_ringKrullDim. This yields dim S = dim R + dim(S/I), directly without localizing.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031E, first sentence (lines 27471--27473), citing Lemma Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total, lines 27420--27456)

proof.text: Choose finite sets x and y generating m_R and m_(S/I), of cardinalities their respective spanFinranks, using Noetherianity [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Lift y along q to a finite subset z of m_S, with q injective on z and image y. Set t = f(x) ∪ z. Its span is I ∨ span(z), so it contains I. Its image under q is span(y) = q(m_S). Equality of ideal images under a surjection gives span(t) ∨ ker(q) = m_S ∨ ker(q); ker(q) = I is contained in both, so span(t) = m_S. Finset cardinal bounds and injectivity on z give spanFinrank(m_S) ≤ card(t) ≤ spanFinrank(m_R) + spanFinrank(m_(S/I)).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031E, lines 27474--27479

proof.text: Regularity of R and S/I identifies their maximal-ideal spanFinranks with their Krull dimensions [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Cast the finite generator bound into WithBot ENat, and use the dimension formula from step 2 to obtain spanFinrank(m_S) ≤ dim S. Apply Mathlib IsRegularLocalRing.of_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_le, whose reverse inequality is Krull's height theorem, to obtain IsRegularLocalRing S. The finite-set construction handles empty generating sets without a separate positive-dimension assumption.
